system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: As of August 2026, may a female employee who has used her full maternity leave take further continuous leave to care for the child? If so, for how many days, in what circumstances, and what document must she produce? Answer briefly, covering all points.
raw_response:
As of August 2026, under Thailand’s Labour Protection Act (amended in 2019), a female employee who has used her full 98 days of paid maternity leave may take an additional unpaid leave of up to 60 days to care for the child, making a total of up to 158 days of continuous leave.

This further leave is available only if the employee has worked continuously for at least one year with the same employer. She must notify the employer in writing of her intention to take this leave and may be required to provide a copy of the child’s birth certificate as supporting documentation.
